title: PostgreSQL Extensions: pg_stat_statements and Performance Profiling
realWorldScenario: Your database CPU is pegged at 95%. Hundreds of different query patterns run concurrently from microservices. You need to identify which queries are consuming the most cumulative time and I/O across the entire server.
questionStatement: Explain how `pg_stat_statements` tracks SQL execution metrics in PostgreSQL. How does it normalize SQL text? Write a query against `pg_stat_statements` to find the top 5 most resource-intensive queries by total execution time, buffer cache miss ratio, and average call latency.
expectedConcepts: Buffer cache hit ratio formula (shared_blks_hit vs shared_blks_read)
Identifying high-frequency N+1 queries vs slow individual queries
hints: Why does pg_stat_statements need to be in shared_preload_libraries?
How does it group queries that only differ by WHERE id = 1 vs WHERE id = 2?
Buffer cache hit ratio = hits / (hits + reads).
